object whose absence is stated; cognition or realization in this context
locative qualifying the stage or context; refers to the beginner level mentioned in the preceding verse
compound adjective with enclitic ca; sandhi niryatnaḥ+ca realized as niryatnaśca in the fused token
optative verb fused with demonstrative pronoun asau; subject is the aspirant in the initial stage

items.question: Can an aspirant at the initial stage become effortless without awakening?
premises: The preceding context affirms duality and bondage-liberation as true for the beginner.
Awakening is presented as a condition relevant to the initial stage.
Effortlessness is considered as a possible state for that aspirant.
items.inference: Without awakening at the initial stage, that aspirant would become effortless, implying effortlessness there depends on awakening rather than arising in its absence.
uncertainties: Whether niryatnaḥ here means free of effort in practice or free of striving due to realization is context-dependent.
The exact referent of asau is inferred from the preceding verse as the beginner aspirant.
items.plain_english: Without awakening at the initial stage, that one would be effortless.
